compliance._status: INERT - no rule may emit a violation until its citation is verified against the primary source.

rules.source: General Financial Rules 2017, Government of India
rules.statement: Procurement above the prescribed value must use open advertised tendering rather than a limited or single-source route.
rules.verification_note: Confirm the clause number AND the current monetary threshold; the threshold has been revised by amendment more than once, so a correct clause with a stale figure is still wrong.

rules.source: General Financial Rules 2017, Government of India
rules.statement: A limited tender enquiry must draw at least the prescribed minimum number of responsive bidders to constitute a competition.
rules.verification_note: Confirm whether the minimum applies to bids invited or bids received - the two give different violation counts on the same data, and only one is the rule.

rules.source: General Financial Rules 2017, Government of India
rules.statement: A utilisation certificate is due within the prescribed period after the sanctioned work concludes.
rules.verification_note: Confirm whether the period runs from completion, from the end of the financial year of the grant, or from date of release. The code assumes completion; the other two shift every result.

rules.citation: CVC procurement guidance on single-tender/nomination awards
rules.statement: An award made without competition must carry a justification recorded on the file.
rules.verification_note: Identify the specific circular and year. This is the weakest citation in the registry - CVC guidance is spread across many circulars and one must be named before this rule can fire.

rules.citation: CPWD Works Manual - administrative approval precedes execution
rules.statement: Execution of a work must not commence before administrative approval and expenditure sanction are in place.
rules.verification_note: Confirm the clause and the manual edition. Note that state PWD manuals govern state works and may differ from CPWD; a record's executing agency decides which manual applies to it.

typologies._status: INERT - every typology awaits source verification. The library defines what to look for and where the definition came from; it asserts nothing about any record yet.

typologies.name: Bid rotation
typologies.subject: VENDOR_PAIR
typologies.description: A stable group of firms bids on the same tenders, taking turns to submit the lowest bid so each wins a share over time.
typologies.signature: The same set of bidders recurs across tenders while the identity of the winner cycles, with each member's win rate close to 1/group size and losing bids clustered just above the winner.
typologies.source: OECD Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement
typologies.verification_note: Confirm the pattern definition and, more importantly, decide the recurrence and clustering thresholds from case evidence rather than by choosing round numbers - an unsourced threshold here reintroduces exactly the problem this layer avoids.

typologies.name: Cover or complementary bidding
typologies.subject: TENDER
typologies.description: Competitors submit deliberately uncompetitive bids so a pre-selected winner appears to have won a genuine competition.
typologies.signature: Losing bids are implausibly far above the winner, or cluster at a near-constant margin, or are submitted by firms that never win anything in the same category.
typologies.source: OECD Guidelines for Fighting Bid Rigging in Public Procurement
typologies.verification_note: Confirm whether the margin test is defined on absolute or relative spread; the two disagree on large-value tenders.

typologies.name: Persistent single-bidder awards
typologies.subject: VENDOR
typologies.description: A firm repeatedly wins tenders that attracted no other responsive bid, in a market where competition would be expected.
typologies.signature: A vendor's share of single-bid awards is far above the base rate for the same scheme, district and value band.
typologies.source: World Bank Sanctions Board decisions; EU single-bidding indicators in public procurement
typologies.verification_note: Single bidding is a red flag, not proof - remote and specialised works legitimately attract one bidder. Confirm the peer base rate is computed within scheme and value band before use.

typologies.name: Award to a sanctioned entity
typologies.subject: VENDOR
typologies.description: A contract is awarded to a firm that appears on a debarment or blacklist at the time of award, or to a successor of one.
typologies.signature: Vendor identity matches a published debarment list entry whose sanction period covers the award date.
typologies.source: World Bank listing of debarred and cross-debarred firms; CVC and state PWD blacklists
typologies.verification_note: This is the only typology here whose evidence is an adjudicated fact about a named entity rather than an inferred pattern, so it is the strongest - but matching must be on identity, not name similarity. A fuzzy name match against a debarment list is a defamation risk, not a finding.

typologies.name: Contract splitting
typologies.subject: TENDER
typologies.description: A work is divided into parts each falling just below a procurement threshold, avoiding open tendering.
typologies.signature: Multiple awards to the same vendor, in the same district and short window, each just below a statutory threshold, whose sum exceeds it.
typologies.source: GFR procurement thresholds; CAG audit findings on splitting
typologies.verification_note: Depends on the same statutory threshold as the compliance registry's open-tender rule. Verify once and share the value - two copies of a legal threshold will drift apart.

typology_reachability._claim_limit: A typology match means the record resembles a pattern proven in adjudicated cases. It is not a fraud finding. Because enforcement data records only CAUGHT fraud, recall against undetected schemes is unmeasurable, and no coverage claim may be made from these detectors.
typology_reachability._subject_warning: VENDOR and VENDOR_PAIR typologies make statements about an entity, never about an individual work. Attributing an entity-level finding to one record would repeat the labelling error that invalidated the previous calibration dataset.
